industry.why: Underweight, from Double Underweight, on the row's own written condition ('to D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or the industry back at C with Online retail holding A'): the tape leg is met, industry relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior) with Online retail A for a third reading. The reasoned read agrees in direction: US consumer confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 (Goldman Sachs, 25-Nov), Goldman's Jaisson (20-Nov) favours Retailers and Bell (20-Nov) wants 'Domestic not Defensive' in the UK, and the 27-Nov-26 regime (risk-off in the open, led by the AI capital-spending unwind and its credit leg) has the consumer away from the epicentre the Double Underweight was set for. Not Neutral because Stehn (Goldman, 22-Nov) expects high energy prices to slow euro area consumption over winter, France is contracting (PMI 46.2) and no European consumer survey was read. The sector rows beneath hold their letters. One live holding (D'Ieteren 2.66%); 20 Pool stocks. Counter-case: lifting a consumer row on the tape in an open risk-off with the European consumer unread is early. Back to F on a European consumer reading that is falling; to C on one that is not falling with Online retail holding A.

sector.why: Underweight, carried: high-multiple platforms hit by the discount rate, property-linked classifieds hit twice; relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). Pool names Trustpilot, Baltic Classifieds. Counter-case: asset-light cash generators are where re-ratings start, and the tape has recovered to C.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. The one Spanish item is sector-level (Kepler constructive on Indra as Spain lifts defence spending, 26-Nov); Iberia's market read arrived unreadable; relative strength is not graded by country. One live holding, Arteche (3.02%). An absence is an absence; no tilt.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
